content: To Open the Solution Container: Peel back the overwrap at the corner and remove the solution container. Some cloudiness or opacity in the plastic may be visible due to moisture absorption during sterilization. This is a normal occurrence and does not compromise the quality or safety of the solution. The opacity will gradually fade over time. 3. To Assemble the Vial and Flexible Diluent Container (Aseptic Technique Required): Remove the protective covers from both the vial and the vial port on the diluent container: For the vial, swing the pull ring over the top of the vial and pull downward to initiate the opening. Then, pull straight up to fully remove the cap. (Refer to Figure 1 and Figure 2.) Important: Once the breakaway cap is removed, do not access the vial with a syringe. For the vial port cover, grasp the pull ring tab, pull upward to break the three tie strings, and then pull back to remove the cover. (Refer to Figure 3.) Screw the vial into the vial port until it is fully tightened. (Refer to Figure 4.) Note: The clicking sound alone does not confirm a seal. The vial must be turned as far as it will go. Once the vial is seated, do not attempt to remove it. Label the container appropriately. 4. To Reconstitute the Drug: Gently squeeze the bottom of the diluent container to inflate the area surrounding the end of the drug vial. With your other hand, push the drug vial downward into the container, causing the walls of the container to telescope. Grasp the inner cap of the vial through the container walls. (Refer to Figure 5.) Pull the inner cap from the drug vial. (Refer to Figure 6.) Confirm that the rubber stopper has been removed, allowing the drug and diluent to mix. Mix the contents of the container thoroughly and use the solution within the specified time frame. Inspect the bottom of the vial to confirm that the stopper has been removed and that the drug and diluent have been fully mixed. (Refer to Figure 7.) If the rubber stopper is not removed on the first attempt and the medication is not released, manipulate the inner cap back into the rubber stopper without removing the drug vial from the diluent container. Repeat the steps for stopper removal and mixing. 5. Preparation for Administration (Aseptic Technique Required): Confirm that the vial contents have been activated and mixed properly. Check the container for leaks by squeezing it firmly. If any leaks are detected, discard the unit as sterility may be compromised. Close the flow control clamp on the administration set. Remove the cover from the outlet port located at the bottom of the container. Insert the piercing pin of the administration set into the outlet port using a twisting motion until the pin is securely seated. Note: Refer to the full instructions provided with the administration set for additional details. Lift the free end of the hanger loop at the bottom of the vial, breaking the two tie strings. Bend the loop outward to lock it in an upright position, and suspend the container from the hanger. Squeeze and release the drip chamber to establish the correct fluid level within the chamber. Open the flow control clamp to clear air from the administration set, then close the clamp. Attach the administration set to the venipuncture device. If the device is not indwelling, prime the set and perform venipuncture. Adjust the rate of administration using the flow control clamp. 6. Warning: Do not use flexible containers in series connections, as this may compromise the sterility and safety of the solution.
